post.caption: Sunlight can fade this pink gem. Kunzite can fade when exposed to heat and bright light. It was found near Pala, California, in 1902, and chemist Charles Baskerville named it after George Kunz of Tiffany. Kunzite is the pink to lilac variety of the mineral spodumene, and trace amounts of manganese give it that color. Its color changes with the viewing direction, an effect called pleochroism, so cutters usually orient it to show the deepest pink through the top. Its hardness is 6.5 to 7, with two perfect cleavage directions. Brazil and Afghanistan are two of its main sources, and the Smithsonian holds an 880 carat heart-shaped kunzite from Brazil.
